title: AI Moves Into CAD Workflows, but the Verified Boundary Remains Narrow
question: What changed, and which developments matter most to this audience?
argument: The consequential change is not a single model breakthrough but the arrival of AI agents at several adjacent engineering handoffs: custom parametric-feature development, simulation setup, and simulation-ready robotics workflows. Onshape and SimScale describe workflows that move natural-language intent into native CAD and analysis operations, while NVIDIA is making the surrounding simulation stack more accessible. For technical leaders, these are credible feasibility signals for constrained internal workflows—not yet evidence that the resulting geometry, analyses, or physical-system behavior are dependable without engineering review.
synthesis: The sources point to a common architectural shift: AI is being placed inside the tools that retain design intent or execute engineering operations, rather than left as a detached conversational layer. Onshape’s proposed text-to-FeatureScript path can make reusable parametric tools; SimScale’s agent claims to carry a CAD model into a solver workflow; NVIDIA’s Newton presentation describes an open simulation layer for physical systems. That connection matters because each integration can shorten a handoff, but it also makes validation at each handoff—the feature definition, solver setup, and eventual physical test—the practical adoption boundary.
limitations: All commercial capability descriptions are vendor or vendor-reported claims, and none supplies a disclosed, independent comparison of generated CAD features or agent-selected simulation setups against engineer-reviewed production outcomes. The robotics sources concern simulation infrastructure and evaluation practice, so they are supporting context rather than proof of CAD or manufacturing-design performance.

claims.statement: Onshape says its FeatureScript MCP Server connects LLMs to Onshape so teams can generate custom features from natural-language requests.

claims.statement: Onshape says the resulting custom features can carry requirements from an LLM request into model-based-definition annotations.

locator.quote: carry requirements from an LLM request into Onshape

claims.statement: Engineering.com reports that SimScale's Engineering AI Agent is available through Onshape's app store and can set up and run simulations from Onshape.
SimScale says that, from one prompt, its agent can propose a setup, mesh geometry, run physics, and return results in Onshape.

locator.quote: propose an appropriate setup, mesh and run the physics

claims.statement: NVIDIA's Newton presentation states that Newton is completely open source.
The Physical AI Podcast reports that a blind hardware evaluation used 10 manipulation tasks, three attempts each, a common time window, and a common scoring sheet.

Embedding agents in CAD and simulation workflows can reduce handoffs, but does not establish that their outputs are production-ready because the cited sources do not report independent checks of feature correctness or solver-setup validity.
